evidence_points: The guidance advises the public how to reduce the risk of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection.
It identifies additional precautions for food handlers, childcare settings and healthcare workers.
It explains that UKHSA performs epidemiological investigations and laboratory typing during outbreaks.
It supports joint investigation of animal- or environment-associated outbreaks with relevant authorities.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary page from UKHSA or another named UK public authority.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.

The source is specific to symptoms, prevention and public-health control of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli and should not be generalised beyond its stated population, disease, setting, period or response function.
Operational use requires confirmation of the current page version, responsible organisations, affected people, setting, timing and supporting evidence.
An alert, test result, symptom report, notification, surveillance count or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation applies.
Final decisions require the current official scope plus exact clinical, laboratory, epidemiological, environmental, operational, communication, governance and review evidence.
